core_summary: In this engaging moral story, a boastful boy named Mario regularly brags about having dozens of friends at school. Observing his grandson's superficial view of popularity, Mario's wise grandfather challenges him to a bet over a bowl of fruit chaat, claiming Mario doesn't have as many real friends as he thinks. The grandfather retrieves a strange 'invisible chair' from the attic, telling Mario that sitting on it will reveal who his true friends are. Excited to prove himself, Mario takes the invisible chair to school. When he attempts to sit on it during recess, he misses the non-existent seat and falls flat on his back twice, causing his classmates to burst into laughter. Undeterred, Mario tries a third time. To his amazement, he remains suspended in mid-air—not because of magic, but because three loyal classmates (Guneet, Asma, and Deepa) physically catch and hold him up. Mario realizes that while many peers are happy to laugh at a fall, only true friends step forward to support you.
key_concepts: Quality vs. Quantity in Relationships: Distinguishing between a large circle of casual acquaintances and a small group of genuinely loyal friends.
Experiential & Pedagogical Testing: Using an engaging, practical experiment (the invisible chair) to help someone discover a life truth for themselves.
Fair-Weather Companionship vs. True Support: Contrasting casual peers who laugh at misfortunes with loyal friends who offer physical and emotional assistance.
Overcoming Public Embarrassment & Resilience: Learning to value genuine support over social popularity and superficial applause.
Intergenerational Wisdom: The role of grandparents in using humor, patience, and creative challenges to guide young people.

key_terms.definition: Expressing excessive pride, self-satisfaction, or vanity regarding one's possessions, popularity, or abilities.
Unable to be seen by the eye; concealed from sight.
Peers who remain close only during pleasant times but abandon you during difficulties.
Held, supported, or hanging in mid-air without touching the ground.
A person one knows slightly, but who is not a close or deeply trusted friend.
A temporary break or period of play between school classes.
A letter group added to the end of a root word to alter its meaning or part of speech (e.g., friend -> friendship).
Continuing steady effort or action despite setbacks, embarrassment, or discouragement.

key_takeaways: True popularity is measured by the loyalty of your friends, not the number of people who know your name.
Real friends reveal themselves through supportive actions during difficult or embarrassing moments.
Do not be discouraged by those who laugh at your stumbles; focus on those who help you stand back up.
Wisdom often comes from experienced elders who guide us with creative, practical life lessons.
Cherish and nurture genuine friendships—they are far more valuable than casual social approval.
